answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity post a small, time-locked stake that is forfeited if peers catch it misbehaving, so a whisper of cheap clones cannot flood the market without real cost. Reputation then accrues slowly, like pigment settling into cloth: a newcomer starts pale and earns deeper colour only through verified work over many epochs. Honest agents that cross the ridge of proven history trade cheaply, while fresh, unproven identities stay throttled until their record is real.
